Disappointing Experience & Trust Issues
Despite informing the class in advance that my child would not be wearing the class T‑shirt, my child was made to sit out for the entire class and was not allowed to dance. The T‑shirt is made of nylon, which is very uncomfortable for children in summer.
A dance class is meant to encourage and teach, not punish or publicly embarrass children. This incident had a negative emotional impact on my child.
What’s more concerning is that when we called the instructor to enquire, a false explanation was given, creating a serious trust issue. Parents expect honesty when it comes to their children.
Additionally, the class cannot complete even one song in a month, which questions the quality of training. Overall, this is not a child‑friendly or transparent environment.

Sincere advise to parents, think 100 times before enrolling and sending to such pathetic class.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
First of all, our dance class is a professional dance institute, and we have been successfully running it for the past 9 years. During this journey, we have provided quality training to 1,200+ students, and even today, several students have been learning with us regularly for the last 8 years, which reflects the trust parents place in our institute.  

Regarding the concern mentioned in the review, your daughter is only 4–5 years old, and you stated that she feels uncomfortable wearing a nylon T-shirt during summer. Had you informed us earlier about this issue, we would have gladly arranged a cotton T-shirt option for her comfort.  

However, the institute T-shirt was purchased at the time of admission, and your daughter has now been attending classes for almost 6 months. During this period, we had repeatedly informed you that the institute T-shirt is mandatory in class, yet on several occasions she was sent in regular home clothes instead.  

As for the training quality, we usually teach one song over the course of one month, which includes 12 structured sessions, not 30 days. Our focus is always on improving the children’s dance techniques, rhythm, body movement, and confidence, so they are able to dance well on any song in the future. To everyone reading this, the issue here is not about the quality of the class, but about personal ego over a small disciplinary action.
